text.p: Andres Galarraga hit a game-tying three-run homer in the bottom of the ninth inning off John Wetteland, who then walked home the winning run to give the Colorado Rockies a 10-9 victory over the Texas Rangers Wednesday.

Ellis Burks led off the inning with a grounder that shortstop Benji Gil threw away for an error. Larry Walker singled before Galarraga launched his 19th homer over the right-field fence, giving the Rockies a 9-9 tie.

"Wetteland is one of the best closers in the league," said Galarraga, who was celebrating his 36th birthday. "Last night he threw me a couple of fastballs high and inside and a slider outside to strike me out. Today he threw me the same way. He threw me fastballs on the hands and I waited for the slider."

"He did a good job of hitting, don't get me wrong," Wetteland said. "But I didn't throw it where I wanted it. Last night I worked him in and when he was fighting him off, that's when I went away with a slider and it worked. Today I tried the same thing and really didn't execute the pitch.
"He did a heck of a job hitting it anyway."

Dante Bichette doubled and Vinny Castilla was intentionally walked. Kirt Manwaring bunted back to Wetteland (4-1), who threw too late trying to force Bichette at third, loading the bases. Wetteland then walked Walt Weiss on a 3-2 pitch.
"I was ready to swing but it was hard and off the plate," Weiss said. "I knew it was going to be hard to get to, so I just let it go. He was busting me hard and I was just trying to survive."
Burks and Bichette also homered for the Rockies, who avoided their first three-game sweep at home this season. Curt Leskanic (1-0), who got the final out in the top of the ninth, was the winner.
The Rangers had their four-game winning streak snapped. They led 7-1 and 9-6 before losing for the first time in 31 games when taking the lead into the eighth inning.
Wetteland blew his fourth save in 19 chances. He has seen his ERA soar from 0.94 to 2.73 in his last two outings.
In Los Angeles, Billy Ashley's pinch-hit, two-run homer in the seventh rallied the Dodgers past the Anaheim Angels 7-5 to sweep the "Freeway Series."
The Dodgers used a trio of two-run homers to take the finale of the two-game set, as Raul Mondesi and Todd Zeile also homered for Los Angeles.

Ashley, pinch-hitting for Nelson Liriano, turned on a 2-2 offering from reliever Mike Holtz (2-1) and drove it 425 feet to the back of the bullpen in left field, scoring Wilton Guerrero and giving the Dodgers a 6-5 advantage.
It was the Dodgers' first pinch-homer of the season, and Ashley's first since last September 25. His five pinch-homers last season tied Lee Lacy for the club record.
Reliever Darren Dreifort (2-0) got the win.
Todd Worrell threw a hitless ninth, posting his 16th save in 19 opportunities for the Dodgers, who have won three straight at home and are 26-7 when scoring four or more runs.
In San Diego, Jose Canseco homered twice and Mark McGwire added his 26th homer of the season as the Oakland Athletics outslugged the Padres 11-9, sweeping their two-game interleague series.
Canseco's second homer of the game and 15th of the season followed McGwire's two-run blast in the third. McGwire's homer left him one behind Seattle's Ken Griffey Jr for the major-league lead.
It was the 46th time that Canseco and McGwire have homered in the same game and second time this season for the A's, who were the last team in the majors to win three straight games.
Carlos Reyes (2-0) allowed a run in one inning of relief and Buddy Groom got the final out for his first save.
Doug Bochtler (0-1) suffered the loss, allowing a run in his one inning of relief.
Ken Caminiti and Rickey Henderson homered for San Diego, which has lost four straight.
The Padres' Tony Gwynn left the game after four innings with a sore right heel, and Caminiti left after the sixth with a strained left hamstring. Both are listed as day-to-day.

In San Francisco, Mark Gardner allowed two runs and three hits over 7 2/3 innings and Stan Javier belted his second homer in as many games as the Giants improved to 5-1 in interleague play with a 4-2 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
Gardner (8-2) also helped himself at the plate, going 2-for-2 with a sacrifice. He has won eight of his last nine decisions and has surrendered four runs or less in all of his 15 starts this season.
Rod Beck gave up a leadoff double to Griffey in the ninth but rebounded to strike out the side and notch his National League-leading 23rd save.
